themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 39 this week—a 700% spike versus the 4.9-complaint weekly average—signaling a sudden, widespread deterioration in road surfaces across Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights that demands immediate investigation into root cause and scope.
evidence: 39 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.9-complaint weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 15.89)
Spike coincides with 324 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, with 287 alteration projects underway—suggesting construction-related street damage
Recurring CB budget request for sanitation equipment/trucks implies chronic street maintenance underfunding
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to document pothole size, location, and damage patterns; cross-reference with active construction sites
Interview DOT officials on emergency street repair protocols and whether recent alterations have triggered damage

themes_detail.label: Blocked driveway parking enforcement breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Blocked driveway complaints surged to 10 this week—a 129% increase from the 4.4-complaint weekly average—suggesting either a sudden wave of illegal parking or a collapse in enforcement capacity this week.
evidence: 10 blocked driveway complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4-complaint weekly baseline (129% spike, z-score 4.27)
Illegal parking overall remains high at 1,128 complaints over 90 days, suggesting chronic parking pressure in the district
Spike appears isolated to this week—not sustained—indicating possible enforcement gap or sudden event
reporting_angles: Check NYPD parking enforcement ticket data for this week to determine if complaints outpace enforcement actions
Interview residents on most-blocked streets to identify problem corridors and repeat offenders

themes_detail.label: Electrical system failures spreading
themes_detail.summary: Electric complaints peaked at 39 two weeks ago—a 152% spike above the 15.5-complaint weekly average—suggesting a district-wide electrical infrastructure strain that may indicate broader utility grid stress or aging building systems.
evidence: 39 electric complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 15.5-complaint weekly baseline (152% spike, z-score 4.9)
Heat/hot water complaints dominate 90-day totals (5,671), suggesting aging HVAC/electrical infrastructure tied to vintage building stock in Morningside Heights
287 active alteration projects may be straining older electrical systems if upgrades are incomplete
reporting_angles: Interview Con Edison about service disruptions or grid stress in the district during the spike period
Survey building owners on whether electrical upgrades are keeping pace with the district's conversion/renovation activity

themes_detail.label: Noise complaints accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints jumped to 18 last week—a 115% spike from the 8.4-complaint weekly average—indicating a sudden rise in either construction/street noise or residential disturbances that warrants identifying the specific source.
evidence: 18 noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.4-complaint weekly baseline (115% spike, z-score 4.68)
Residential noise (1,502 complaints over 90 days) and street/sidewalk noise (374) combined represent significant quality-of-life concern
324 recent DOB permits with 287 active alterations likely contributing to construction-related noise
reporting_angles: Break down last week's 18 noise complaints by type (residential vs. construction) and location to pinpoint source
Identify which construction projects were actively demolishing or renovating that week

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk/street cleanliness deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints reached 9 last week—a 213% spike from the 2.9-complaint weekly average—combined with street sweeping complaints up 500% two weeks ago (3 vs. 0.5 average), signaling a sanitation service breakdown that aligns with the district's recurring budget requests for more sanitation trucks.
evidence: Sidewalk condition: 9 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9-complaint weekly baseline (213% spike, z-score 3.79)
Street sweeping: 3 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5-complaint weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Community Board has repeatedly requested new sanitation trucks/equipment, indicating chronic underfunding of street maintenance
reporting_angles: Request DSNY street sweeping schedule data for the district to identify service gaps or route changes during the spike period
Interview residents on most-neglected blocks and photograph conditions to document the complaint trend
